---
title: "M0 ignition training"
execute:
  eval: false
---

M0 detects the transition from background activity to sustained seasonal
activity. Training selects decision thresholds using historical seasons while
preserving the information boundary at every issue week.

## Workflow

```{r}
library(PAGe)

historical <- load_flu_hist("/authorized/path/flu_history.csv") |>
  prepare_surveillance_data()
selection <- validate_season_selection(
  historical,
  training_seasons = development_seasons,
  exclude_seasons = excluded_seasons,
  holdout_seasons = "2025-26"
)

tuning <- tune_m0(historical, selection = selection)
validate_m0_tuning(tuning)
draft_m0 <- fit_m0(historical, selection, config = tuning$best_params)
m0 <- freeze_m0(draft_m0, tuning = tuning)
```

The tuning objective should be computed from held-out seasons. Manual ignition
labels may define the target used for evaluation, but they must not be exposed
as features to the held-out detector. Report early and late detection errors
separately; a mean error alone can hide operationally different failure modes.
`fit_m0()` returns a draft; only `freeze_m0()` produces an artifact that M1 may
consume. `build_m0()` remains available for legacy callers.

## Grid expansion

Check every genuinely tuned M0 axis after validation. If a probability
threshold wins at an edge, add one adjacent probability step while keeping the
value inside its valid domain. Keep `n_consec`, `K_sum`, `N_req`, `w_min`, and
`w_max` integer-valued and preserve their logical and operational constraints.
Rerun the same LOSO seasons and lexicographic score.

Do not optimize only the mean error. Review maximum error, missed detections,
and early versus late errors by season. A detection-window edge can be accepted
only when it is an intentional operational constraint; otherwise the optimum
has not been bracketed.

## Runtime checks

At deployment, retain the weekly detector snapshots rather than only the final
ignition week. Confirm that each snapshot contains no observations after its
issue week and that a manual override, when used, is explicit and auditable.
The plotting functions in the M0 reference section compare weekly detector
state with historical truth and help diagnose unstable threshold behavior.
